string: Language for Horizon labels, Settings, and Quick Menu. Auto follows the game language.
The interface language Starfield was using when Horizon started.
Shows extra on-screen info about the scanner and compass to help track down a problem.
Measures how long the HUD takes to update and saves it so a problem can be found.
Switches which HUD test runs. Ordinary play uses Baseline.
Saves one performance report the next time you apply settings.
These stay off while you play. Turn them on only if something needs checking.

Click a key chip to bind. Esc cancels. Backspace or Delete clears. A clash (another slot, the settings key, or a game control) is warned and ignored. Tiles are slots 13 through Slot Count, wrapped by Slots per Row. Slots 1-12 keep the game's own favorite keys. If Extended Mode is off or paused, the grid is grayed and saved keys are kept.

Shows extra yellow text on the HUD about the crosshair, the weapon in your hands, what the compass sees, and environment keys. Compass icons also get small numbers. You see this on screen as soon as it is on. Turn it on only while you are tracking down a HUD problem, then turn it off so the extra text does not stay.

Measures how long the HUD takes to update and keeps those timings so a slowdown can be found. You will not see a new panel on screen; the numbers are stored for a report. Ordinary play should leave this off. Turn it on only when you need a timing report, then turn it off. Saved looks do not change this.

Switches which HUD test runs while Advanced Performance Timing is on. Baseline is ordinary play and is the one to use unless you were asked to try a specific test. Hover Skip turns off Horizon hover cards and scanner drawing (the game's own hover can still show). Fixture shows a test stand-in instead of live loot, people, or ships. Full Pipeline, Same Target, Rapid Targets, Scanner, and Backgro...

Saves one performance report the next time you press OK. Leave this off for ordinary play. Turn it on, press OK, play for a short while, then turn it off again. Nothing is saved until you apply settings. Needs Advanced Performance Timing to be on.
Debug Overlay, Advanced Performance Timing, Perf Mode, and Arm Perf Dump stay off during ordinary play. Support can turn them on if something needs checking.
Turns the jetpack, health, and oxygen into slim strips. Mouse and keyboard only; this switch stays in the header so it is always in reach.
Size of the slim jetpack, health, and oxygen strips when Compact Mode is on. Follow HUD uses the overall HUD size. Custom sets a size just for those strips.
Turns the health and oxygen card on or off. When it is on, Show when still decides the moments it appears, so an On switch with a Show when rule is not broken.
When the vitals card appears. Always keeps it visible. HP or O2 below full shows it only when health or oxygen is not full. It can also show only in combat, or hide while you are in your ship.
Vertical stacks health above oxygen. Horizontal puts oxygen beside health on one row.
Full keeps separate health and oxygen cards. Compact uses the same slim boost, health, and oxygen card as Compact Mode. If either Compact Mode or this Compact choice is on, that merged card shows.
When the equipment card is hidden, the vitals card slides to the exact center. After you move vitals in Arrange Cards, this is ignored.
A green sliver ahead of the health bar while health is coming back.
Turns the boost card on or off. Show when still decides the moments it appears.
When the boost card appears. In use / not full shows it while you are boosting or boost is not full.
Turns the afflictions card on or off.
When the afflictions card appears. Only when afflicted shows it while you have an injury or effect.
How affliction chips are arranged: a column, a row, or icons only.
A small card that turns red while a hazard is hurting you and green while suit protection is restoring.
A soft pulse at the edges of the screen when health or oxygen is very low. The center of the view stays clear.
Turns the equipment card (weapon, ammo, grenades, Starborn power) on or off.
Crosshair off? Set this to ALWAYS or COMBAT ONLY.
Shows grenade count and the selected Starborn power on the equipment card. Off hides those extras and also hides the game's leftover grenade and power clips so no stray line stays on the HUD.
Enemy health at the top center. Turns off the game's own enemy bar while this is on.
A stealth pill above the crosshair while you sneak. Turns off the game's own stealth meter while this is on.

When the center aiming reticle shows. Always is the default. When weapon drawn shows it only with a weapon out. Off hides the reticle only; prompts, target cards, hit markers, the kill X, the damage ring, and the stealth pill stay.
Look of the reticle while you look at something you can use: the game's ring, a Horizon dot, a Horizon cross, or none.
A hit mark and a kill X at the crosshair. Turns off the game's own markers while this is on.
Floating damage numbers. Turns off the game's own numbers while this is on.
A ring around the crosshair that shows where damage came from. Turns off the game's own arcs while this is on.

While you aim down a scope, the hold-breath prompt is a Horizon chip with an oxygen meter. Off uses the game's own prompt. Needs the Scope module. If Scope is not installed, this row stays locked and the game's prompt is used. Saved preference is kept.
Size of the hold-breath chip. 1.00 matches the game's prompt. Use plus and minus for a precise size.
Puts the hold-breath chip back at the game's spot and size.
Turns the Horizon compass on or off.
Master switch for markers on the Horizon compass. Quest objectives still show while this is on.
Markers for your follower and companions on the compass.
Color of follower and companion markers on the compass.
Location, point-of-interest, and outpost markers on the compass.
Your ship and vehicle on the compass.
Your custom map marker on the compass.
Turns the quest tracker on or off.
How wide the quest tracker is. Font size stays the same. A narrower card wraps the objective onto more lines.
How tall the quest tracker may grow. Extra lines stop at this height.
When on, long quest text starts a new line instead of ending in an ellipsis.
Turns the planet card on or off.
Adds a gravity and air line under the planet name.
While exposure to heat, cold, radiation, or other hazards builds up, the planet card gets a pulsing amber outline.
Turns the character card (level, XP, credits, mass) on or off. When it is on, Show when still decides the moments it appears. Off hides the card completely, including after XP or a level up.
When the character card appears. Event choices show it for a few seconds after XP, a level up, credits, or a skill point, and can also show when you are overweight.
How many seconds the character card stays up after an event. This is used only when Show when is an event choice. It does nothing when Show when is Always.

Wrist watch in the lower left. Off hides it. Vanilla is the game's watch. Vanilla + Horizon keeps the game's watch and paints it with Horizon colors. Horizon digital is a number readout. Horizon analog is a clock face. Use Off if you never look at it. Use Horizon digital if you want a clear time at a glance.

Horizon's card for the activate prompt and item hover (name, keys, value). Off uses the game's prompt exactly, including the game's name bar and key boxes. Turn this off if you want the original look. Turn it on for Horizon's target card.
Compact is one line: icon, name, and key. Full is the taller card.
Size of activate prompts, loose-item cards, compare cards, and enemy tags.
Where hover cards sit. Crosshair keeps them by the reticle. Follow target sits them next to the object on screen.
Shows value and weight on the item hover card and on the selected container row.
Size of the full container item list.
How solid the container list and crosshair item cards are. This is separate from HUD card opacity.
The ring and line the game draws around the object you look at. Off never shows it. Containers only shows it on a container list. Vanilla is the game's own drawing.
While you are in a vehicle, the hold-to-exit prompt is a Horizon pill. Off uses the game's prompt. Move it in Arrange Cards.

The game's quick menu (favorites cross) as Horizon cards in your colors and font. Off is the game's look. This switch is the enable. Turn it on if you want the Horizon favorites menu. Turn it off to keep the original cross. Extended Mode stays muted until this is on.

Off is the game's 12-slot T. On is up to 24 slots. Paused if another favorites add-on is installed; saved On/Off is kept. Slots 1-12 still use the game's own favorite keys. Turn this on after Horizon Style if you want extra slots and key chips.
How many slots show when Extended Mode is on, 12-24. The key grid shows slots 13 through this number. Default 24. Lowering the count only hides extra tiles; keys and items are kept.
4, 6, or 8. Default 6. The key grid wraps to this many tiles per row. Use 4 on a small screen, 8 if you want fewer rows to scroll.

Cross + Bars keeps the vanilla T for slots 1-12 and puts Horizon slots in bars underneath. Bars draws every slot in rows. Use Cross + Bars if you still want the familiar T. Use Bars for a simple grid.
SHOW = unused extras appear as empty squares with a faint plus. HIDE = leave them off until assigned. Occupied extras always show, and inventory assign still shows empties so you can pick one.
How solid the extra window is. It does not change other HUD cards. Applies the next time you open the Quick Menu.
Extra slot size compared with slots 1-12; 1.0 is the same size. Applies the next time you open the Quick Menu.
Clears every extra-slot key. The slots still work from the menu.
A short +XP note beside the character card. With Horizon messages installed, the game's own +XP popup is hidden while this is on. Off keeps the game's popup (or none, if the game would not show one).
Replaces the game's quest banner with a Horizon toast. Move it in Arrange Cards.
How many seconds each mission toast stays on screen.
How many mission toasts may stack at once.
Size of the mission toast. Follow HUD uses the overall HUD size.
The quest sound comes from the game's banner and always plays. It cannot be turned off here.
Restyles companion 'liked that' lines as a Horizon card. English game text only for now; other lines stay the game's.
Small label above the game's other notices. None shows just the message. Data or Misc adds that label. Applies from the next message.

Color of highlights, switches, selected rows, and this window. Pick a named color for a ready-made look, or Custom to mix your own. The whole settings screen follows this color as soon as you change it. Use a brighter accent if cards feel hard to see, or a calmer one for long play sessions.

Your own accent color as six digits (red, green, then blue). Type them after the hash. An incomplete or invalid color keeps the last good one. Use this when none of the named colors match what you want. This is not a file name and not a setting key — it is only the color.

Fill color of HUD cards and this window. Pick a named color, or Custom to mix your own. Light fills switch the text to dark so labels stay readable. Use a dark fill for night scenes and a light fill if you want a paper look.
How solid HUD cards are. Values above 1.00 stay fully solid and then push the fill darker or brighter. This is not the same as Card background.
How see-through the card fill is, from clear at 0 to solid at 100. This is direct transparency and is separate from Card opacity, which can go above 1.00.
Strength of the shadow under HUD cards. 0 is none. 12 is the built-in look. 100 is a strong shadow.
How see-through this settings window is. 30 is the lightest. 100 is solid.
Font for Horizon text. Exo 2 is the default. If a Horizon font is not installed, the game font is used and your choice is kept.
Size of Horizon text, on top of HUD scale.
Auto uses dark text on light card colors. Light and Dark force one tone.
Card titles in spaced capital letters, or in title case with tight spacing.
A soft drop shadow under HUD text. Helps on bright scenery; off is sharpest.
Size of every Horizon card that follows the HUD. A card with its own Custom size no longer follows this.
Gap between the screen edge and the cards. Cards you moved in Arrange Cards keep their distance from this line.
Your vertical resolution so crosshair cards land on whole pixels and stay sharp. Off skips snapping.
Horizon bars glide to a new value instead of jumping. Health bars also keep a short fading ghost of what you just lost.
Cards fade and slide when they appear or hide, instead of popping.
Out of combat (and not at low health) HUD cards fade toward Dim opacity.
How far cards fade out of combat. Lower is fainter.
Time on the planet card: off, local planet time, your PC clock, or both.
12-hour or 24-hour clock for local, game, and PC time.
Celsius or Fahrenheit on the planet card and scanner.
Plays a short HORIZON UI welcome after you load a save. It never pauses the game and never takes input.
The key that opens this window. A new key takes effect after you restart the game.

Language for Horizon labels, Settings, and Quick Menu. Auto follows the game language detected when Horizon started. Changing this and pressing OK reloads the table once. Game item names and the game's own $ tokens stay in the game language. HUD card words still use English until later localization work.
The interface language Starfield was using when Horizon started. This line is read once at init and does not change until you restart the game. It does not follow the override below.
When on, new HUD messages are stored in the log. When off, nothing new is stored. Messages still show on screen.
When on, the log is saved on disk. Turning this off only stops writing; existing files are not deleted.
How many messages to keep per character.

Opens the Message Log folder in Explorer (the same folder the game writes when Save to disk is on). The path is shown in Setting Details after you press SHOW. The folder is not created if Save to disk has never been on. Use this to copy or back up log files.

Opens the Message Log folder in Explorer so you can see log files from other characters. Each character is a separate file in that folder. Search and pins still live inside the in-game log window. This does not switch the character you are playing.
Opens the in-game message log. Type filters, search, pins, and clear stay inside that window. This is not the disk folder — use Folder SHOW for Explorer.

Changes how far the scanner can outline and scan things. Vanilla leaves the game as it is. 2x, 3x, and 5x multiply that distance, never past 500 meters. A long reach can cost frame rate in busy areas. Applies the next time you open the scanner.

How far from the screen center the scanner picks up and outlines things. This does not change how far away you can scan (that is Scan reach). Small is about half the game's circle. Vanilla leaves the game's cone: Horizon writes nothing, so the game or another highlight-radius mod stays. Large reaches the top and bottom. Wide reaches the left and right. Full screen covers the corners too. Applie...
How thick scanner outlines are. Vanilla keeps the game's own look. Thick is one and a half times. Thicker is twice. Applies the next time you open the scanner.
Hides ordinary Horizon HUD cards while the hand scanner is open. Item cards, the container list, the activate prompt, and combat feedback always stay.
Hides the watch while the hand scanner is open. Shared clocks on the planet card are unchanged.
Hides quest popups and the mission toast while you scan. This belongs with messages and works even when the scanner add-on is not installed.
Dims the trait popup while you scan. This belongs with messages and works even when the scanner add-on is not installed.
How dim the trait popup is while you scan.
Opens a mock scanner on the HUD so you can drag panels and the kept vitals, then save.
Puts scanner panel spots, sizes, and compact forms back to their defaults. Other Horizon settings are kept.
Puts every scanner setting back to its default. Cards, look, and message settings are kept.
Opens Size and Placement so you can change the shared HUD scale.
Opens Size and Placement so you can change the shared screen margin.
Opens Clocks and Units, which the watch and planet card also use.
Opens Scanner HUD for hiding the watch while you scan.
Drag HUD cards on screen. Save keeps the new spots. Arrange is always in the header, including while you search, so you can jump to layout without leaving the finder.

Turns the scanner's nearby-signal list on or off. On shows what the scanner has found around you (flora, fauna, resources, and similar pings). Off hides that list so the scanner view is quieter. Saved preference is kept if the Scanner module is not installed.
Size of the signal list. Follow HUD uses the shared HUD scale. Custom sets a size just for this list. Use Custom when the list is hard to read or covers too much of the view.

How many signals the list may show at once. A lower number keeps the list short in busy areas. A higher number shows more finds before older ones drop off. This does not change how far the scanner can see.
Shows your ship and vehicle on the scanner so you can find them while you scan. Off hides those markers if you want a cleaner scan view.
Shows a small compass while the scanner is open so you can keep your heading. Off hides it. The main HUD compass is a separate switch under Cards.
Size of the scanner compass. Follow HUD uses the shared HUD scale. Custom is only for this compass.
Shows place names on the scanner (settlements, outposts, and similar labels). Off hides those names so the view is only outlines and signals.
Internal compact form for the signal list. Kept in the settings file; not shown here because Compact-all already covers it.
Internal compact form for the scanner compass. Kept in the settings file; not shown here because Compact-all already covers it.
Internal size for place-name tags. Kept in the settings file; move scanner panels in Arrange Scanner instead.
Internal highlight for the nearest unscanned find. Kept in the settings file; not shown here.
Internal world-marker drawing while you scan. Kept in the settings file; not shown here.

How dialogue options the game has already used are shown. Dimmed: they stay in the list, faded. Hidden: they leave the list (numbers 1-9 and the count only include what is still shown; if every option was said, all come back). Tagged: they stay, faded, with a SAID chip. Persuasion lists never hide options. Use Dimmed if you still want to pick an old line. Use Hidden for a shorter list. Use Tagg...

How persuasion options are marked. Chip: a small tag beside the line. Colored text: the line itself uses the persuasion color. None: no extra mark (the game's own look). Use Chip if you want a quick scan of which lines are persuasion. Use Colored text if you dislike extra tags. Use None to stay close to the game.
Color of the persuasion mark when the tag is a chip or colored text. Pick a named color so persuasion lines stand out from ordinary choices. Ignored when Persuasion tag is None.

On: Horizon draws the persuasion score, the highlighted reply, and remaining turns in place of the game's bars. Off: the game's own meter is used. Turn this on for a meter that matches Horizon dialogue. Turn it off if you prefer the original bars.
Experimental question and advance markers on dialogue options. This game version has no marker data, so the switch stays off and does nothing. Your saved choice is kept for a later game update.

When on, Horizon pauses its own subtitles if another subtitle add-on is installed, so the two do not overlap. This is the default. Turn it off (or press Use Horizon) only if you want Horizon's subtitles on top of that other add-on. Saved preference is kept.

When on, Horizon pauses its own dialogue list if another dialogue add-on is installed, so the two do not overlap. This is the default. Turn it off (or press Use Horizon) only if you want Horizon's list from the next conversation. Saved preference is kept.

Horizon found another subtitle add-on (such as Enhanced Subtitles) and paused Horizon subtitles so the two do not overlap. Use Horizon turns auto-pause off (SubAutoPause=0) so Horizon's subtitles show again. This only works if Horizon's HUD messages file is the one installed.

Horizon found another dialogue add-on (such as Enhanced Dialogue Interface) and paused Horizon's dialogue list. Use Horizon turns auto-pause off (DlgAutoPause=0). The change applies from the next conversation.
Whether Horizon is drawing subtitles right now. Active means Horizon's subtitles are on. Paused means another subtitle add-on was found and auto-pause is on.
Whether Horizon is drawing the dialogue list right now. Active means Horizon's list is on. Paused means another dialogue add-on was found and auto-pause is on.
Core HUD is always installed with Horizon. It draws the vitals, compass, quest tracker, and the other HUD cards. There is nothing to add or remove here.
The Horizon font pack (Exo 2 and friends). Installed: Horizon text uses the font you pick under Appearance. Not installed: the game font is used and your font choice is kept.

Quick Menu restyles the favorites cross and can add extra slots. Installed: the Quick Menu page is live. Not installed: the game's favorites menu is used. Installed - disabled: Horizon Style is off. Paused - conflict: another favorites add-on is in the way of Extended Mode.

Comms and Dialogue restyles subtitles, the dialogue list, mission toasts, and companion reaction cards. Installed: those pages are live. Not installed: the game's own look is used and your saved choices are kept. Paused - conflict: another subtitle or dialogue add-on was found and auto-pause is on.
Scanner restyles the hand scanner. Installed: Scanner pages are live. Not installed: the game's scanner is used and your saved choices are kept.
Scope restyles the hold-breath prompt while you aim down a scope. Installed: Combat > Scope is live. Not installed: the game's prompt is used and your saved choice is kept.
Notifications records HUD messages into the Message Log. Installed: Message Log pages are live. Not installed: nothing is written to disk from this menu.

Installed means the add-on's files are in this load order. Enabled means you turned that add-on's own switch on (for example Horizon Style). Visible means a card is allowed to appear by its Show when rule. A module can be installed and still look off because a switch or a Show when rule is hiding it.
Opens Cards > Status so you can set when vitals and other cards appear. Show when is per card: Always, only in combat, only when not full, and similar rules.
Opens Mission Toasts and Reaction Cards, which also need the Comms module.

Turns Horizon subtitles on or off. On draws spoken lines as a Horizon card. Off uses the game's subtitles (or another add-on's). Use On for Horizon's look. Use Off if you already have a subtitle add-on you prefer.
Turns the Horizon dialogue list on or off. On draws replies as Horizon cards. Off uses the game's dialogue menu (or another add-on's). Applies from the next conversation.
Shows the speaker's name above the subtitle. Off is the line only. Use On in busy scenes so you know who is talking.
Gives the speaker name its own small card in dialogue. Off draws the name as plain text. Use On to match other Horizon cards.
Size of subtitle text. About 1.00 is the usual size. Raise it if lines are hard to read. Lower it if the card covers too much of the scene.
How wide the subtitle card is, as a percent of the screen. Wider wraps less often. Narrower keeps more of the scene visible.
On draws a panel behind the subtitle. Off is text only, with a soft dark outline. Use Off for a quieter picture. Use On for contrast on bright worlds.
Shape of the reply list. Card list is Horizon's stacked cards. Compact is a tighter stack. Classic centered is closer to the game's centered list. Use Compact on smaller screens.
How many replies show at once. All fits every option on the card. A number caps the list and can show an N more hint. Use a cap if a long list covers the speaker.
Key hints under the dialogue card. Horizon is a restyled strip. Game bar is the original. Hidden draws no strip (the keys still work). Use Hidden if you already know the keys.
Replaces the game's quest banner with a Horizon toast. Off uses the game's banner. Move the toast in Arrange Cards. Needs the Comms module.
Restyles companion 'liked that' lines as a Horizon card. English game text only for now; other languages stay the game's. Needs the Comms module.

This add-on is listed in the Horizon UI installer. Installed means its files are loaded. Not installed means the game's own look is used. Paused - conflict means another add-on was found and Horizon stepped aside. Saved choices are kept either way. You can add the add-on from the Horizon UI installer.
No other subtitle or dialogue add-on was found. Horizon is drawing its own subtitles and dialogue.

The optional Quick Menu (Favorites) module replaces Interface\favoritesmenu.swf and favoritesmenu_lrg.swf. If you use another favorites or quick-menu mod, untick Quick Menu (Favorites) on the Optional Modules page. A Vortex update that reuses earlier choices may untick it; re-tick it to k...

Installs the Horizon fonts (Exo 2 and Roboto, SIL OFL 1.1): Interface\fonts_horizon.swf and Interface\fontconfig_en.txt. This replaces any other font mod's fontconfig_en.txt. Enables the font options in the F11 settings window.

Installs no font files and leaves your current fontconfig (vanilla or another font mod) alone. Horizon UI falls back to the game font, and the font options in the F11 settings window will be grayed out.
Horizon UI's standard settings. Moragar's Choice won't be in F11's Presets list.

Starts you on the author's own settings, matching the Nexus screenshots. Only applies if you don't already have saved Horizon settings; your existing settings are never overwritten. Also adds Moragar's Choice to F11's Presets list so you can apply it any time. If you skip it, it won't be in the list; reinstall and pick it to add it later.

Horizon-styled quick menu, the favorites cross (Interface\favoritesmenu.swf + _lrg). Replaces the game's quick menu and any other mod that replaces those files. Ticked by default; untick this to keep the game's quick menu or another mod's. A Vortex update or reinstall that reuses your earlier choices may untick this; re-tick it to keep Horizon's quick menu. Unticked, F11 > CARDS > QUICK M...

Horizon-styled subtitles and speaker card (Interface\hudmessagesmenu.gfx + _lrg). The next page lets you choose whether to also install the Horizon dialogue menu, which replaces other dialogue menu mods. Conflicts with other subtitles mods and any other mod that replaces hudmessagesmenu: install one or the other. Not ticked by default if one of them is detected. Modules you don't install appear...

Horizon-styled hand scanner (Interface\monoclemenu.swf + _lrg). Replaces the game's scanner and the scanner of other scanner mods: let Horizon overwrite them (load Horizon after them). Hides the Horizon HUD while scanning (F11 > SCANNER). Scanner popup options need Comms.

Horizon-styled hold-breath prompt for weapon scopes (Interface\scopemenu.swf + _lrg): a chip with a target icon, the label and an O2 meter that turns yellow / red at the HUD's low-O2 levels; move and size it in ARRANGE CARDS. The game's own prompt is hidden, never removed, and the scope works as before. It replaces the game's scope menu, so it is ticked by default: if you use another scope mod,...
Adds the Message Log to the F11 menu.

Installs the Horizon dialogue menu (Interface\dialoguemenu.swf + _lrg and the comms_dialogue marker). It replaces any other dialogue menu mod. If the installer detected one (this option is then not pre-selected): another dialogue mod was found. Horizon dialogue replaces it; pick this to replace, or Skip to keep it. Ship hail menus are not changed.
Skip Horizon dialogue (use if another dialogue mod is installed)

Installs only the Horizon subtitles half of Comms and no dialogue files. Keeps your other dialogue mod or the vanilla dialogue menu. The dialogue section of the F11 COMMS tab stays locked. Recommended when another dialogue mod is found.

Loose files: add bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 (and sResourceDataDirsFinal=) under [Archive] in Documents\My Games\Starfield\StarfieldCustom.ini. Credits: Exo 2 by Natana...
